statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.

statute.display_text: Wrath (Ira). The third terrace, Purg. XV-XVII. Love perverted. The penitent walks through thick, blinding, choking smoke.
statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.
source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

The Inferno's fifth circle holds the wrathful too (Inf. VII-VIII), but as incontinence under Aristotle's scheme rather than as an item on this list. The overlap of four sins with circles 2-5 is a coincidence of the two vocabularies, not a correspondence.

statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第7圈第3环，Inf. XIV-XVII。罪：亵渎者、鸡奸者、放高利贷者。刑（contrapasso）：灼热的沙地上永落火雨：亵渎者仰卧，鸡奸者不停奔跑，放贷者蹲坐，颈上挂着钱袋。

The descent out of this ring is on Geryon's back (Inf. XVII), which is how the eighth circle is entered.

statute.text_en: Avarice (Avaritia), with prodigality beside it. The fifth terrace, Purg. XIX-XXII. Love excessive. The penitent lies face down on the ground.

source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

The terrace holds the prodigal as well as the miserly (Purg. XXII), so this article is not 'stinginess' but disordered attachment to goods in either direction — the same pairing the Inferno's fourth circle makes of the avari and the prodighi.

statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第4圈，Inf. VII。罪：吝啬者（avari）与挥霍者（prodighi）——两群人，不是一条罪。刑（contrapasso）：分作两半圈推着巨大的重物对撞，撞上便互相咒骂，再各自转回去重来。守卫：Plutus。
statute.text_en: The fourth circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. VII. The miserly (avari) AND the prodigal (prodighi) — two crowds, not one sin. Two half-circles rolling great weights against each other, colliding, reviling each other, and turning back to do it again. Guarded by Plutus.

The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.
source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

The terrace holds the prodigal as well as the miserly (Purg. XXII), so this article is not 'stinginess' but disordered attachment to goods in either direction — the same pairing the Inferno's fourth circle makes of the avari and the prodighi.

statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第2圈，Inf. V。罪：情欲之罪（Inf. V.63-65 举出克娄巴特拉与海伦）。刑（contrapasso）：被永不止息的狂风卷着吹打，如生前被情欲卷走一般。守卫：Minos。
statute.text_en: The second circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. V. The carnal, who subjected reason to appetite. Swept forever on a wind that never rests, as appetite swept them. Guarded by Minos.
statute.display_text: The second circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. V. The carnal, who subjected reason to appetite. Swept forever on a wind that never rests, as appetite swept them. Guarded by Minos.
statute.source: Dante, Inferno IV-XXXIV — the nine circles, the three gironi of the seventh, the ten bolge of Malebolge and the four zones of Cocytus. The layering is Aristotle's tripartition as Virgil states it at Inf. XI.79-84 (incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade), NOT the seven capital sins, which order the terraces of Purgatorio and are corpus DEADLY_SIN. Primary text quoted from the Longfellow 1867 translation, Project Gutenberg #1001, public domain. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §2, §2.1, §3.1, §6.
source_notes: This is a circle of hell, not a terrace of Purgatory. The seven capital sins do not stratify the Inferno: pride, envy and sloth get no circle at all, and the four that seem to line up with circles 2-5 do so because 'incontinence' and those four are adjacent vocabularies, not because Dante mapped them. The seven belong to corpus DEADLY_SIN, EU-DS-T1..T7, and no article in either corpus cites the other's coordinate.

ATTESTATION IS MIXED AND IS RECORDED PER ARTICLE IN payload['attestation']. The structure — the three headings and the division at the wall of Dis — is PRIMARY: Inf. XI.79-84 in a public-domain translation, quoted in verify-christian-structure.md §2. The detail on each place — canto range, sinners, contrapasso, guardian — is SECONDARY: Wikipedia's Inferno article cross-checked against UT Austin's Danteworlds (Guy P. Raffa), agreeing with each other and with the nine realm descriptions this deployment already had (§2.2 checks all nine and finds none of them false). The report could not reach Digital Dante (Barolini) or the Dartmouth Dante Project (§7) and therefore asserts nothing about what any commentator says; neither does any article here.

Minos stands at this circle's entrance and assigns every soul its circle by coiling his tail that many times (Inf. V.4-12). He is the sorting mechanism of the whole Inferno and he is posted HERE, not at the ninth circle.

statute.title_zh: 第八圈·欺诈（恶囊 Malebolge，十囊）
statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第8圈，Inf. XVIII-XXX。罪：对无特殊信任关系者行欺，分作十道同心的石囊（bolge）。刑（contrapasso）：十囊各有其刑，见本圈十条子条文。守卫：Geryon。
statute.text_en: The eighth circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. XVIII-XXX. Fraud worked on those bound by no special trust, in ten concentric stone pouches (bolge). Each pouch has its own; see the ten articles under this one. Guarded by Geryon.

Fraud is graver than violence in this poem, and the reason is stated rather than implied: it corrupts the bond peculiar to man (Inf. XI.22-27). A system that sorts by how much harm was done cannot express that, which is what tests/test_european_hell_basis.py pins.
Cantos XVIII-XXX are thirteen of the Inferno's thirty-four — the largest single stretch of the poem, and the part this deployment had flattened into one realm with one label.

payload_json.conjecture: CONJECTURE — the ordinal, not the place. Dante names all four zones (Caina, Antenora, Tolomea, Giudecca) and the travellers cross them in that order in Inf. XXXII-XXXIV, but he does not number them the way he numbers the seventh circle's three gironi (Inf. XI.28-33) or the eighth's bolge. The index 1-4 carried here is the order of descent and is this corpus's arrangement; the names and the betrayed bonds are the poem's.

statute.text_zh: 傲慢（Superbia）。炼狱山第一层，《炼狱篇》X-XII。属「爱之偏邪」——爱指向邻人之恶。苦修：背负巨石弯腰而行，沿途是刻在石上的谦逊范例。
statute.text_en: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.display_text: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.
source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

Gregory the Great treats superbia not as one of the seven but as the root they grow from (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87: 'Radix quippe cuncti mali superbia est'). Dante gives it a terrace, and the lowest; the ordinal here is Dante's, not Gregory's.

statute.text_en: The second circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. V. The carnal, who subjected reason to appetite. Swept forever on a wind that never rests, as appetite swept them. Guarded by Minos.

statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第7圈第3环，Inf. XIV-XVII。罪：亵渎者、鸡奸者、放高利贷者。刑（contrapasso）：灼热的沙地上永落火雨：亵渎者仰卧，鸡奸者不停奔跑，放贷者蹲坐，颈上挂着钱袋。
statute.text_en: The third ring (girone) of the seventh circle, Inf. XIV-XVII. Blasphemers, sodomites and usurers. A burning sand under a rain of fire: the blasphemers lie supine, the sodomites run without stopping, the usurers crouch with purses at their necks.

This article is the only place in the database where this part of the poem exists. It is deliberately NOT a request to create seventeen realms: a realm is a destination souls are routed to, and nothing here can decide which subdivision a soul belongs in.

BLASPHEMY IS HERE, AND IT IS NOT HERESY. The heretics are the sixth circle; blasphemy is violence against God and belongs to this ring. Reading one as the other is the shape of mistake 8308204 was withdrawn for, and tests/test_european_hell_basis.py names it as such.
The descent out of this ring is on Geryon's back (Inf. XVII), which is how the eighth circle is entered.

statute.text_zh: 傲慢（Superbia）。炼狱山第一层，《炼狱篇》X-XII。属「爱之偏邪」——爱指向邻人之恶。苦修：背负巨石弯腰而行，沿途是刻在石上的谦逊范例。
statute.text_en: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.

statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第4圈，Inf. VII。罪：吝啬者（avari）与挥霍者（prodighi）——两群人，不是一条罪。刑（contrapasso）：分作两半圈推着巨大的重物对撞，撞上便互相咒骂，再各自转回去重来。守卫：Plutus。

statute.text_zh: 傲慢（Superbia）。炼狱山第一层，《炼狱篇》X-XII。属「爱之偏邪」——爱指向邻人之恶。苦修：背负巨石弯腰而行，沿途是刻在石上的谦逊范例。
statute.text_en: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.

statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

statute.text_zh: 傲慢（Superbia）。炼狱山第一层，《炼狱篇》X-XII。属「爱之偏邪」——爱指向邻人之恶。苦修：背负巨石弯腰而行，沿途是刻在石上的谦逊范例。
statute.text_en: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.display_text: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.
source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

Gregory the Great treats superbia not as one of the seven but as the root they grow from (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87: 'Radix quippe cuncti mali superbia est'). Dante gives it a terrace, and the lowest; the ordinal here is Dante's, not Gregory's.

statute.text_zh: 傲慢（Superbia）。炼狱山第一层，《炼狱篇》X-XII。属「爱之偏邪」——爱指向邻人之恶。苦修：背负巨石弯腰而行，沿途是刻在石上的谦逊范例。
statute.text_en: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.display_text: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.
source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

Gregory the Great treats superbia not as one of the seven but as the root they grow from (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87: 'Radix quippe cuncti mali superbia est'). Dante gives it a terrace, and the lowest; the ordinal here is Dante's, not Gregory's.

statute.text_zh: 《地狱篇》第2圈，Inf. V。罪：情欲之罪（Inf. V.63-65 举出克娄巴特拉与海伦）。刑（contrapasso）：被永不止息的狂风卷着吹打，如生前被情欲卷走一般。守卫：Minos。
statute.text_en: The second circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. V. The carnal, who subjected reason to appetite. Swept forever on a wind that never rests, as appetite swept them. Guarded by Minos.
statute.display_text: The second circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. V. The carnal, who subjected reason to appetite. Swept forever on a wind that never rests, as appetite swept them. Guarded by Minos.
statute.source: Dante, Inferno IV-XXXIV — the nine circles, the three gironi of the seventh, the ten bolge of Malebolge and the four zones of Cocytus. The layering is Aristotle's tripartition as Virgil states it at Inf. XI.79-84 (incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade), NOT the seven capital sins, which order the terraces of Purgatorio and are corpus DEADLY_SIN. Primary text quoted from the Longfellow 1867 translation, Project Gutenberg #1001, public domain. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §2, §2.1, §3.1, §6.
source_notes: This is a circle of hell, not a terrace of Purgatory. The seven capital sins do not stratify the Inferno: pride, envy and sloth get no circle at all, and the four that seem to line up with circles 2-5 do so because 'incontinence' and those four are adjacent vocabularies, not because Dante mapped them. The seven belong to corpus DEADLY_SIN, EU-DS-T1..T7, and no article in either corpus cites the other's coordinate.

ATTESTATION IS MIXED AND IS RECORDED PER ARTICLE IN payload['attestation']. The structure — the three headings and the division at the wall of Dis — is PRIMARY: Inf. XI.79-84 in a public-domain translation, quoted in verify-christian-structure.md §2. The detail on each place — canto range, sinners, contrapasso, guardian — is SECONDARY: Wikipedia's Inferno article cross-checked against UT Austin's Danteworlds (Guy P. Raffa), agreeing with each other and with the nine realm descriptions this deployment already had (§2.2 checks all nine and finds none of them false). The report could not reach Digital Dante (Barolini) or the Dartmouth Dante Project (§7) and therefore asserts nothing about what any commentator says; neither does any article here.

Minos stands at this circle's entrance and assigns every soul its circle by coiling his tail that many times (Inf. V.4-12). He is the sorting mechanism of the whole Inferno and he is posted HERE, not at the ninth circle.

Fraud is graver than violence in this poem, and the reason is stated rather than implied: it corrupts the bond peculiar to man (Inf. XI.22-27). A system that sorts by how much harm was done cannot express that, which is what tests/test_european_hell_basis.py pins.
Cantos XVIII-XXX are thirteen of the Inferno's thirty-four — the largest single stretch of the poem, and the part this deployment had flattened into one realm with one label.

statute.text_zh: 傲慢（Superbia）。炼狱山第一层，《炼狱篇》X-XII。属「爱之偏邪」——爱指向邻人之恶。苦修：背负巨石弯腰而行，沿途是刻在石上的谦逊范例。
statute.text_en: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.display_text: Pride (Superbia). The first terrace of Mount Purgatory, Purg. X-XII. Love perverted — turned toward a neighbour's harm. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility.
statute.source: Dante, Purgatorio X-XXVII — the seven terraces of Mount Purgatory, the one structure in the Commedia that the seven capital sins order. The sequence is Dante's own, resting on the theory of disordered love Virgil states in Purg. XVII, and is NOT Gregory the Great's: his seven (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87) are inanis gloria, invidia, ira, tristitia, avaritia, ventris ingluvies, luxuria, with superbia their root and not one of them. docs/lore-verification/verify-christian-structure.md §3.3.
source_notes: This is a terrace, not a circle. Dante layers hell on Aristotle's tripartition — incontinenza / malizia / matta bestialitade, said by Virgil at Inf. XI.79-84 — and pride, envy and sloth get no circle in it at all. The withdrawn EU-DS-01..07 carried a `dante_circle`; no such coordinate exists in Dante and it is not restored here.

`opposing_virtue_*` is from the 'seven contrary virtues', a pairing that descends from Prudentius' Psychomachia (c. 410). It is a common later table whose wording varies between versions — charity or kindness against envy — not a list the Church defined, and not one Dante publishes; he names exempla on each terrace instead.

Gregory the Great treats superbia not as one of the seven but as the root they grow from (Moralia in Job XXXI.xlv.87: 'Radix quippe cuncti mali superbia est'). Dante gives it a terrace, and the lowest; the ordinal here is Dante's, not Gregory's.

suggestions.title: Gluttony
suggestions.text: The third circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. VI. The gluttonous. Lying in cold and filthy sludge under a ceaseless fall of hail, foul water and snow. Guarded by Cerberus.

suggestions.title: Violence
suggestions.text: The seventh circle of Dante's Hell, Inf. XII-XVII. The violent, divided into three rings (gironi) by whom the violence was done to: neighbour, self, or God, nature and art. Each ring has its own; see the three articles under this one. Guarded by the Minotaur.

suggestions.title: Violence against Neighbour
suggestions.text: The first ring (girone) of the seventh circle, Inf. XII. Murderers, plunderers and tyrants. Sunk in Phlegethon, the river of boiling blood, each to the depth his guilt fixes; the Centaurs shoot any who rise higher. Guarded by the Centaurs — Chiron, Nessus, Pholus.

suggestions.title: Violence against Self
suggestions.text: The second ring (girone) of the seventh circle, Inf. XIII. Suicides, and those who squandered their own substance to ruin. The suicides are grown into thorn trees whose leaves the Harpies feed on, and who can speak only from a wound; the squanderers are run down and torn apart by black bitches. Guarded by the Harpies.
